pr1462.body:
Closes #1460
Refs #1309

## Goal
The peer collaboration rules name only herdr-core. A session reads one command per rule and no runtime selection. Owner decision: [scope change](https://github.com/Ancienttwo/repo-harness/issues/1460#issuecomment-6586257628) (clean cut, no compatibility).

## Scope
Rule text only: `assets/reference-configs/global-working-rules.md` (Peer Harness Collaboration) and its synced mirror `docs/reference-configs/global-working-rules.md`. Not in this PR (#1482 owns them): the `repo-harness-herdr-portal` rule and skill, the herdr skill, `herdr-notify.md` and its Herdr Dispatch section. No code.

## Changes
- The runtime selection rule is gone. The first rule now says: use herdr-core, `hc` for terminals and `herdr-app do` for tabs and panes; `hc --help` and `herdr-app commands` are the syntax authority. It keeps the [Runtime commands](https://github.com/Ancienttwo/repo-harness/blob/main/docs/reference-configs/herdr-notify.md#runtime-commands) link and the nested refusal: `HC_TERMINAL_ID` with `HERDR_ENV=1` set, refuse and report.
- Each rule names only the herdr-core command: target by `hc` address or name, `hc send <t>`, start a collaborator with `herdr-app do` and address it with `hc`, `hc read <t>`, `herdr-app do pane.close --pane <pane>`. The classic `herdr` commands, the session-context clause and the workspace-grouping clause are removed.
- Pane layout rule stays: at most 3 panes side by side; split only with `herdr-app do pane.split --direction right`; never split down; a full tab gets a new tab with `herdr-app do tab.new`.
- The missing-runtime rule: a missing or unusable herdr-core stops terminal collaboration; no fallback to tmux or to classic Herdr.
- The issue-flow rule keeps its Herdr Dispatch link and names "the herdr-core commands".
- Unchanged: the `repo-harness-herdr-portal` rule.

## Architecture slice
Architecture slice unchanged, see #1460.

## Verification
Run on `15e34af89` after `git merge origin/main` (macOS Darwin 25.5.0, bun 1.4.3):
- `bun run check:reference-configs` — projection OK, 22 docs (mirror written with `bun run sync:reference-configs`)
- `bun run test:files tests/global-working-rules-distribution.test.ts --timeout 60000 --max-concurrency 1` — 25 pass, 0 fail
- `bun run check:type` not run: text-only change.
- Command names checked against `hc --help`, `herdr-app commands` (`pane.split` takes `right`) and the herdr-core table in `herdr-notify.md`.

## Test changes
None. The pinned phrases in `tests/global-working-rules-distribution.test.ts` (pane layout, `herdr-notify.md#herdr-dispatch` link) stay in the text. No assertion changed.

Test budget: `git diff --numstat main...HEAD -- tests` = 0 added lines; `-- src scripts` = 0 added lines. No test file added.

## Risk and rollback
Risk: Low. The text reaches users' managed `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` blocks through `update`. A session on classic Herdr gets no peer command from these rules and must stop with a clear error; this is the owner's decision. `herdr-notify.md` still describes both runtimes until #1482 lands. Rollback: `git revert <merge commit>`.

pr1491.body:
## Goal
Add one herdr-core transport. Every repo-harness call to herdr-core goes through a typed `hc` CLI call with `--json`, and pane placement goes through `herdr-app do`. Every call is scoped to repo-harness terminals. The module implements decision 1 and the label rule of decision 2 in the [#1474 decision](https://github.com/Ancienttwo/repo-harness/issues/1474#issuecomment-6585114904). It also owns the one repo-harness label set that #1476-#1479 import ([scope change](https://github.com/Ancienttwo/repo-harness/issues/1475#issuecomment-6585272186)). Callers move to it in #1476-#1479.

Refs #1474
Refs #1475 (closes when merged: Closes #1475)

## Scope
New module `src/effects/terminal/herdr-core.ts` and its test `tests/effects/herdr-core-transport.test.ts`. No caller changes. `src/effects/terminal/herdr.ts` stays; the last caller PR deletes it. No JSON-RPC client. In `.archcontext/`, only the `source.include` lists change, for this PR's own file ([decision](https://github.com/Ancienttwo/repo-harness/issues/1474#issuecomment-6585632789)); #1483 owns node summaries and rewrites.

## Changes
- **Typed calls only.** The one hc executor is private. The exported calls are `hcRun`, `hcList`, `hcListAsync`, `hcEvents`, `hcGet`, `hcLabel`, `hcSend`, `hcRead`, `hcWait`, `hcKill`, `hcRm` and `herdrAppDo`. Each runs its program with no shell; addresses and argv go after `--`.
- **Scope (decision 2).**
  - Lists and streams (`hcList`, `hcListAsync`, `hcEvents`) and `hcRun` need a label set with at least one `repo-harness.*` key.
  - Calls on one terminal (`hcGet`, `hcSend`, `hcRead`, `hcWait`, `hcKill`, `hcRm`) take only an hc address: `t`, then 1-9, then base-30 symbols `0-9bcdfghjkmnpqrstvwxyz` (`t7`, `t1b`; hc 0.1.16 `terminals.rs` `id_shaped`). hc never reuses an address on its core, and no name has this shape; a name can name a later terminal. They run `hc get` first and refuse a terminal without a repo-harness label (reason `unowned`), so send, kill and rm never reach a personal terminal.
  - `hcLabel` is the one call on an unlabeled terminal. It is for the `t<n>` that `herdrAppDo('tab.new' | 'pane.split')` just returned, and its result must carry a repo-harness label.
- **Label set, one source.** `RH_LABEL` holds the keys `repo-harness.role`, `.task`, `.request`, `.repository`, `.harness` and `.notify`. `RH_ROLE` holds the role values `notify-relay` and `task-session` ([scope change](https://github.com/Ancienttwo/repo-harness/issues/1475#issuecomment-6585316669); a new role is added here). `RH_NOTIFY_LABELS` is `repo-harness.notify=on`. `RH_NOTIFY_RELAY` is the relay name `rh-notify-relay` and its role label. An unknown `repo-harness.*` key, an unknown role and a notify value other than `on` are refused. Other namespaces (for example Herdr.app's `herdr.space`) pass through. Keys match `^[a-z][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$`; values are printable ASCII.
- **Decoded terminal.** `run` and `ls` rows give `address`, `name` and `state`; hc omits `name` for an unnamed terminal, and it reads as `null`. `hcGet`, `hcLabel` and `hcKill` return the address, name, state, labels, OSC 7501 status, turn, program `pid`, `foreground` process (`pid`, `name`, `argv`, `cwd`) and end `reason` ([decision](https://github.com/Ancienttwo/repo-harness/issues/1475#issuecomment-6585340296)). One rule covers every field that the hc schema does not require: an absent field is undefined (`null` for `pid`, `foreground`, `reason`), and a present field must have the schema type. Status `app` and `msg` are strings; `kind` is a string or null. A wrong type fails with `invalid_response`.
- **Send, read, wait.** `hcSend` returns `{started, turn}`; hc refuses a blocked program with exit 9. `hcRead(t, lines)` returns `{text, complete, why}`: `complete` is false when part of the asked text may be missing, and `why` names the reason (`working`; hc 0.1.17 adds `blocked` and `error`) or is `null` ([decision F1](https://github.com/Ancienttwo/repo-harness/issues/1474#issuecomment-6587630628)). `hcWait(t, seconds)` passes `--timeout` to hc and sets the process timeout to that wait plus the transport timeout; it returns `{ended, reason, turn, status}`.
- **Lifecycle.** `hcRun` takes `noParent` (`--no-parent`), so the notify relay outlives the terminal that starts it. `hcKill` returns the terminal; `hcRm` returns the removed address.
- **All terminals.** `hcList` and `hcListAsync` take `all` (`hc ls --all`), which adds finished terminals; the repo-harness label filter rule is unchanged ([decision](https://github.com/Ancienttwo/repo-harness/issues/1476#issuecomment-6588336229)).
- **Async list.** `hcListAsync(labels)` runs `hc ls` with async `execFile`, the same timeout and SIGKILL, and returns the same summaries, so `operator serve` makes no sync process call ([decision](https://github.com/Ancienttwo/repo-harness/issues/1475#issuecomment-6585405948)). One exit mapping (`settle`) serves the sync and async calls.
- **Stream.** `hcEvents` returns `{close, done}`. It calls back with the first snapshot, each `event` (its `data` is an object, or `null` for a `foreground` change with no foreground process), and a `missed` item (`{seq, terminals}`) when the subscriber fell behind; the consumer replaces its state with it. Heartbeats (every 15 s) are consumed and never reach the callback. Any other line fails with `invalid_response`. The stream has no command timeout. `done` resolves on `close()` or exit 0. It rejects with a `HerdrCoreError`, or with the error that the callback threw; either stops the hc child.
- **One timeout.** `HERDR_CORE_TIMEOUT_MS` = 10 s, per call overridable. The child is killed with SIGKILL.
- **One error type.** `HerdrCoreError` with `program` (`hc` or `herdr-app`) and `reason`:

  | Reason | Cause |
  |---|---|
  | `missing` | The program is not on `PATH` (ENOENT). |
  | `timeout` | The call passed the timeout. |
  | `failed` | Non-zero exit or signal. Keeps `exitCode`, hc's `error.kind` and its message. |
  | `invalid_response` | Exit 0, but the output is not the expected JSON shape. |
  | `nested` | `HC_TERMINAL_ID` and `HERDR_ENV=1` are both set. Checked before any spawn. |
  | `invalid_labels` | No repo-harness key, or a malformed or unknown label. Checked before any spawn. |
  | `invalid_address` | The address is not `t<n>` (a name, `machine/t<n>`, `t0`). Checked before any spawn. |
  | `unowned` | The terminal has no repo-harness label. Found by `hc get`; nothing else runs. |
- **API generation.** hc 0.1.16 reports no API generation in its CLI output (`hc schema` says "Protocol generation 1", but `--json` replies do not carry it). The shape validation in this module is the only guard against a changed hc. A changed shape fails closed with `invalid_response`.
- **Core selection.** The environment selects the core (`HC_SESSION`, `HC_SOCKET`; default `process.env`).

### hc and herdr-app surface used
Read from `hc --help`, `hc <cmd> --help`, `hc schema` and `hc --skill` (hc 0.1.16; the readiness floor is 0.1.17, with the same CLI surface per the #1474 decision), and `herdr-app commands` and `herdr-app --skill` (herdr-app 0.1.11).

| Call | Schema method | Result read |
|---|---|---|
| `hc run --json --bg --label k=v --name --cwd [--no-parent] -- argv` | `terminal.run` | `address`, `name`, `state` |
| `hc ls --json --label k=v [--all]` (`hcList`, `hcListAsync`) | `terminal.list` | `terminals[]`: `address`, `name`, `state` (no labels in rows) |
| `hc get --json -- <t>` | `terminal.get` | `address`, `name`, `state`, `labels`, `status`, `turn`, `pid`, `foreground`, `reason` |
| `hc label --json -- <t> k=v` | `terminal.label` | as `get` |
| `hc send --json -- <t> <text>` | `terminal.send` | `started`, `turn` |
| `hc read --json --lines N -- <t>` | `terminal.read` | `text`, `complete`, `why` |
| `hc wait --json --timeout S -- <t>` | `terminal.wait` | `ended`, `reason`, `turn`, `status` |
| `hc kill --json -- <t>` | `terminal.kill` | as `get` |
| `hc rm --json -- <t>` | `terminal.rm` | `removed` |
| `hc events --json --label k=v` | `events.subscribe` | line 1 `{channel, seq, terminals[]}`, then `{jsonrpc, method, params}` lines: `event` `{seq, terminal, type, data}`, `heartbeat` `{seq}`, `missed` `{seq, terminals[]}` (hc 0.1.16 `events.rs`) |
| `herdr-app do tab.new\|pane.split\|pane.close '<json>'` | Herdr.app commands | created IDs, for example `{pane, terminal}` |

Exit codes: hc writes `{error: {kind, message, hint}}` to stderr. Probed: 0 success, 1 `name_taken` and `live` (`rm` on a live terminal), 2 `usage`, 3 `not_found`, 6 `invalid_params` (`hc run --name -x`). Documented: 7 `needs_target`, 9 `blocked`, 10 `status_mismatch`, 11 `finished`, 124 `run` wait timeout (not reached, because `hcRun` uses `--bg`). `herdr-app do` writes `{"error": "..."}` to stdout and exits 1. The transport keeps the exit code and kind as data and does not branch on a specific code; callers decide.

## Verification
At `20e2cbd21`, macOS (Darwin 25.5.0), bun 1.4.3:
- `bun run check:type`: pass.
- `bun run test:files tests/effects/herdr-core-transport.test.ts --timeout 60000 --max-concurrency 1`: 9 pass, 0 fail, 125 expect() calls. Fake `hc` and `herdr-app` on a scratch `PATH`, with one reply per subcommand, cover:
  - success: `hcRun` (labels and `--no-parent`), `hcList` and `hcListAsync` (a row without `name`; `all` adds `--all` and decodes a finished row; `all` with no repo-harness label is refused), `hcGet` (all decoded fields, `kind: null`; address `t1b`), `hcLabel`;
  - one terminal: `hcSend`, `hcRead` (a partial read: `complete: false`, `why: working`), `hcWait`, `hcKill` (reply without `foreground` gives `foreground: null`, `reason: killed`) and `hcRm`, each after one `hc get` (argv asserted);
  - timeout (sync and async), hc error with exit 3 and `not_found` (sync and async), non-JSON output, seven malformed terminal fields (labels, pid, foreground, reason, status `app`, `kind`, `msg`), an rm reply without `removed`;
  - a missing program (`hc` and `herdr-app`);
  - scope: the nested refusal, six label refusals, five invalid addresses (`rh-worker`, `vps/t3`, `t0`, `t1a`, `-t4`) for get, kill and rm with no spawn, and an unlabeled terminal refused as `unowned` for get, kill, rm and send, where only `hc get` ran;
  - `herdr-app do` success and error;
  - the event stream: snapshot, heartbeat (not passed on), missed, event, a `foreground` event with `null` data, close; a non-JSON line and an unknown method fail with `invalid_response`; a throwing callback rejects `done` with its own error.
- Real smoke, not in CI: hc 0.1.16 (and hc 0.1.17 for `hcRead`: `complete: true`, `why: null`) in a private core (`HC_SESSION`, `HC_SOCKET`, scratch HOME, TMPDIR and XDG paths; the core was stopped at teardown; the owner's core was not used). An unlabeled `hc run --name personal cat` was refused by `hcGet` and `hcKill` (`unowned`) and stayed live; `hcGet('personal')` gave `invalid_address`. On a labeled terminal, `hcRun` with `noParent`, `hcList`, `hcListAsync`, `hcSend`, `hcRead`, `hcWait` (`ended: false`, `timeout`), `hcLabel`, `hcRm` on a live terminal (exit 1, `live`), `hcKill` (`foreground: null`, `reason: killed`) and `hcRm` behaved as the fakes assume. `hcEvents` saw only the labeled terminal. With `HC_HEARTBEAT_MS=1000`, five runs kept the stream up past 3.5 s of heartbeats and delivered `created`, `foreground` (once also the `null` one), `finished` and `removed`; `close()` resolved `done`. Addresses reached `t1n`, and `hcKill` and `hcRm` worked on it. `herdr-app do` was not run against the owner's window; its error shape comes from `herdr-app do nosuch.cmd` (exit 1, stdout JSON).
- Test budget: `git diff --numstat origin/main...HEAD -- tests` 196 added; `-- src scripts` 404 added (0.49:1). One new test file, because no test file owns this new module.

### Review rounds
Round 3 (gatekeeper, `fa9f1248d`) closed every round 1 and 2 finding and found rv1491-r3-events-heartbeat; the earlier thread on `ce2f5b560` reported the same defect. `297505784` fixes it. The same push fixes three decoder gaps that real hc runs found: an unnamed terminal's `name` in `run` and `ls` rows, base-30 addresses, and `null` foreground event data. Each would break a caller in normal use.

Rounds 1 and 2 at `ce2f5b560`:
Round 1 (gatekeeper) and round 2 (Codex) failed. `fa9f1248d` fixes every finding: rv1491-r1-unlabeled-act and cx1491-unscoped-terminal-access (scope above), cx1491-status-fields-not-validated and rv1491-r1-status-decode (one optional-field rule), rv1491-r1-kill-rm-untested (the earlier body claimed kill and rm tests that the file did not have; they exist now), rv1491-r1-events-callback-throw, rv1491-r1-exit-code-list (exit 6) and rv1491-r1-api-generation (recorded above).

### Architecture model
- ChangeSet `rh-1475-herdr-core-include` (archctx 0.11.1) adds `src/effects/terminal/herdr-core.ts` to `source.include` of `capability.runtime-harness.task-agent-host` and `component.task-agent-host.primary`, next to `herdr.ts`. `preview.ownershipDelta`: 1 file became owned (`herdr-core.ts` → `component.task-agent-host.primary`); 0 contested, 0 owner changes, 0 unowned.
- Receipt (unsigned, `approvalAuthenticity: unverified`): journal `changeset_28330365-cbaf-4da0-a959-109c9f3376eb`, base model `sha256:b0936e3f78ee6ee8821ec3b55d5daf9566a8c3675785cf651ed9bdb7443e76f5`, result model `sha256:58ab686860a4e5f2f9990a3785438a28bb38d2d59b0c18903401edd1b3a8e7d7`. Files: `capability.runtime-harness.task-agent-host.yaml` `sha256:c66bbdcf61464489ab68caf98ed11441a7308f39b02cf6d693ecc015be7a044b`; `component.task-agent-host.primary.yaml` `sha256:cd05d8f11bab87f5910e95418d215f899d653b475c46d9cfe3b552b38970ee56`; `.archcontext/generated/ARCHITECTURE.md` (generated, not committed).
- `archctx validate`: valid, 0 errors. `capability-resolver match --path src/effects/terminal/herdr-core.ts`: `capability.runtime-harness.task-agent-host`. `capability-resolver validate`: OK. `bun run check:state-boundaries`: OK (531 files).
- Projection preview for `docs/architecture/modules/runtime-harness/task-agent-host.md` changes only the matched-prefix lines (header and §1.3). The rolling writer publishes them after merge.
- Archimap: not refreshed. `measure.ts --map docs/architecture/archimap.html --model .archcontext/model/nodes` reports 0 uncovered, unknown, duplicate or undocumented nodes, 0 overlaps and 0 unassigned files. The new file falls in the existing `effects` map module. An include-only change moves no map module, node, relation or flow.

Architecture slice unchanged, see #1475.

## Risk
High tier (runtime host contract). No caller uses the module yet, so this PR changes no runtime behavior. The contract risk is for #1476-#1479: the result shapes come from hc 0.1.16, and a later hc that changes them fails closed with `invalid_response`. Each call on one terminal costs one extra `hc get`. The ownership check and the act are two hc calls; another API client can remove the labels between them, but it cannot give the `t<n>` to another terminal.

## Rollback
Revert the commits of this PR. No caller imports the module; the reverted include lines leave no owner gap, because the file goes with them.

## Goal

CI must have a pinned, checksum-verified `hc` before #1476 moves `tests/herdr-task-lifecycle.test.ts` to herdr-core. Classic herdr stays installed until #1481. The pin is hc 0.1.17 ([scope change](https://github.com/Ancienttwo/repo-harness/issues/1490#issuecomment-6587635684), [decision](https://github.com/Ancienttwo/repo-harness/issues/1474#issuecomment-6587630628)).

## Scope

- In scope: the herdr-core pin in `.ai/harness/policy.json` and its two seed projections, a new install action, the three CI jobs that install classic herdr, the external-tooling doc, and the pin tests.
- Not in scope: the classic action and `external_tooling.herdr` (#1480, #1481), strict readiness (#1480), test moves to hc (#1476).

## Changes

- `.ai/harness/policy.json#external_tooling.herdr_core`: `min_version` 0.1.16 → 0.1.17, and new `release_assets` with URL and sha256 for `linux-x86_64`, `macos-aarch64` and `macos-x86_64` at 0.1.17. Readiness keeps `min_version` as a floor; CI installs exactly that version.
- `src/effects/adoption/standard-plan.ts` and `scripts/lib/project-init-lib.sh`: the same block, so the downstream seed stays equal to the pin.
- New `.github/actions/install-pinned-herdr-core/action.yml`, the same shape as the classic action. It reads the version, URL and digest from the pin, downloads the tarball, verifies sha256 (a mismatch exits non-zero before extract), extracts `herdr-core`, installs it as `hc`, prints `hc --version`, checks it equals `hc <min_version>`, and adds the directory to `GITHUB_PATH`.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: `native-oar`, `verify` (affected shards) and `test` (daily functional) run the new action directly after the classic install. `verify` and `test` run the lifecycle test on Linux, so they need `hc` too.
- `docs/reference-configs/external-tooling.md` and its `assets/` copy: CI now installs hc from the pin; the CI tests stay classic-only.

### Release source

herdr-core has no GitHub release objects, only tags. Its official channel is the release server that `distribution/install.sh` reads (`curl -fsSL https://releases.herdr.dev/core/install.sh | sh`). The upstream `release.yml` builds each target from a `v*` tag and uploads the tarballs and `manifest.json` to `releases.herdr.dev/core/<version>/`.

- Manifest: https://releases.herdr.dev/core/0.1.17/manifest.json (`version` 0.1.17, `generation` 1)
- Installer: https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr-core/blob/master/distribution/install.sh
- Release workflow: https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr-core/blob/master/.github/workflows/release.yml

On 2026-11-03 I fetched the manifest, downloaded the three tarballs into a `mktemp -d` directory, and ran `shasum -a 256`. Each local digest equals the manifest digest:

| Asset | sha256 (local = manifest) |
|---|---|
| `herdr-core-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | `82ec44043f6894bfdb716b979b87cda43fd7fa46b0104e7b7bd93e64d1a9b877` |
| `herdr-core-macos-aarch64.tar.gz` | `cedbd4d4d9ba1385588198dd4d3c67d2654478f33add5b6445d4d0eb9da5fcf3` |
| `herdr-core-macos-x86_64.tar.gz` | `e2dc3211edb1f1c77d0e73dd76c1426636d71050f34a5303916a56d363d7062b` |

Architecture slice unchanged, see #1490.

## Verification

Head `a331018da` (main merged at `76dea5a2c`), macOS 26.5 arm64, Bun 1.4.3, after `bun install --frozen-lockfile`:

- `bun run check:type`: exit 0.
- `bun run test:files tests/herdr-runtime-pin.test.ts tests/check-ci-job-split.test.ts --timeout 60000 --max-concurrency 1`: 80 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail; 55 pass, 0 fail. The skip is the existing `aliasCheckoutIsTemporary` case, because the checkout is under `/tmp`.
- `bun run test:files tests/check-agent-tooling.test.ts --timeout 60000 --max-concurrency 1 -t herdr-core`: 4 pass, 0 fail.
- `bun run test:files tests/bootstrap-files.test.ts tests/cli/adoption-plan.test.ts tests/ci-documentation-consumers.test.ts tests/create-project-dirs.runtime.test.ts --timeout 60000 --max-concurrency 1`: 14, 59, 5 and 15 pass, 0 fail (seed projections equal the pin).
- Not run locally: the full affected lane. PR CI runs it in three shards and is the authority.
- PR CI [run 41519741642](https://github.com/Ancienttwo/repo-harness/actions/runs/41519741642) at `a331018da`: Required / CI pass. The "Install pinned herdr-core runtime" step prints `herdr-core-download.tar.gz: OK` and `hc 0.1.17` in all four Native OAR legs (macOS) and all three affected shards (Linux).

Changed test data and assertions:

- `tests/check-ci-job-split.test.ts`: the exact native-oar step order now lists `Install pinned herdr-core runtime` between the classic install and the test step, because this PR adds that step.
- `tests/herdr-runtime-pin.test.ts`: `min_version` is expected to be 0.1.17, the new pin.
- `tests/check-agent-tooling.test.ts`: the fake `hc` in the `present` and `configuration-error` cases prints `hc 0.1.17`. The `present` case models an hc at the policy floor; with the floor at 0.1.17, `hc 0.1.16` reports `unavailable`. No assertion changed.

Test budget: 60 added test lines (`tests`), 30 added product lines (`src`, `scripts`): 2.0:1, at the cap. No new test file. The action and workflow (40 lines) are outside the measured roots.

## Risk

High tier: a `.github/` workflow change and a pinned binary download.

- Supply chain: the URL and digest come from the upstream manifest and match a local download. The action fails closed on a digest mismatch, so a changed upstream file cannot install.
- Availability: `releases.herdr.dev` is a new download host for CI. If it is down, the three jobs fail at the install step. `curl --retry 3` covers short faults.
- Readiness: a local hc below 0.1.17 now reports `unavailable` for the optional `runtime.herdr_core`. Strict readiness does not depend on it.
- Classic herdr stays on PATH in the same jobs, so the existing tests do not change.

## Rollback

Revert this PR. The classic action and pin are unchanged, so CI returns to the classic-only state.

Refs #1474
Closes #1490

## Goal

Blocked and done notices reach the Bot webhook, Slack, Discord and Telegram on herdr-core. Decision 6 on #1474 (option A): a repo-harness relay reads `hc events --json --label` and posts the existing `repo-harness.bot-event/v1` envelope.

Refs #1474
Closes #1479
Depends on #1491 (base branch `feat/1475-hc-transport`).

## Scope

In: the relay, `herdr notify install|start|uninstall|relay`, the notify install record, the operator notify status and collector, the notify relay section of the Bots page (console canvas 1793648307-5702, decision https://github.com/Ancienttwo/repo-harness/issues/1474#issuecomment-6586831326), the compile-required operator edits that the decisions on #1479 allow, removal of the classic plugin and the Clef shadow decision, the `source.include` footprint in the architecture model, the notify reference doc, CHANGELOG.

Not in: the herdr section of Bot access (#1478); summaries, node rewrites and the archimap refresh (#1483). `src/cli/index.ts` changes only the doctor port wiring (boundary decision https://github.com/Ancienttwo/repo-harness/issues/1479#issuecomment-6588828605).

## Changes

- `src/effects/terminal/notify-relay.ts` (new): `repo-harness herdr notify relay --home <path>` follows `hc events --json --label repo-harness.notify=on` (`RH_NOTIFY_LABELS`). It keeps the name, labels and 7501 `app`/`kind` of each terminal from the snapshot, `created`, `labels` (a terminal labeled after start arrives with its `record`) and `status` events. A `missed` item (hc dropped events for a slow subscriber) replaces all held terminal state, and the relay ignores events at or below its seq. On a `turn` event with state `blocked` or `done` it sends one bot event. `task`, `request_id` and `repository` come only from the `repo-harness.task`, `.request` and `.repository` labels. Channels run in parallel and independently (G31). Each hc turn is sent at most once per channel: a successful channel does not send the same terminal, turn and state again, and the next turn is sent at once. A turn event without a turn number is logged and not sent. The relay writes the newest result of each channel to `notify-deliveries.json` (mode 600). It reads the config on each event through `decodeNotifyConfig`, the one decoder of `notify.env`: HTTPS URLs without user information, a Bot URL and key, a complete Telegram target, done flags of `0` or `1`. An invalid config sends nothing, and the log names the broken rule without its value. When the stream ends on its own, it exits 1 and does not restart (decision 6).
- `src/cli/commands/herdr.ts`:
  - `install` takes no `--session` and no Clef options. It checks its input with `decodeNotifyConfig`, lists live relays, writes `~/.repo-harness/herdr/notify.env` (600), starts the relay with `hcRun({noParent: true})` only when none is live, and writes the install record last.
  - `start` (new) is the one manual restart command. It needs a written `notify.env`, starts the relay only when none is live, and writes the install record.
  - `uninstall` lists relays with `hc ls --all`, runs `hcKill` for each live relay and `hcRm` for every relay, also finished ones, then removes the three files.
  - `notifyRelayDoctorCheck` (new): the `herdr-notify-relay` check of `repo-harness doctor`, read-only. `na` without an install record, `ok` when the relay is live, `warn` `relay_stopped` with `repo-harness herdr notify start`, `warn` `hc_unavailable`. `src/cli/commands/doctor.ts` is core, so `DoctorPorts.notifyRelayCheck` carries it and `src/cli/index.ts` wires it.
  - `herdr decision label` is removed.
- `src/effects/terminal/herdr-notify-install.ts`: `relayIsLive` is the one live-relay rule of the status reader and doctor. Private files are read synchronously (each is at most 64 KiB), so the sync doctor and the async status share one reader. The record is `{protocol: 2, kind: 'notify_relay_install', name, labels}` with `RH_NOTIFY_RELAY` values. Any other record, including the classic session record, is `invalid` (fail closed, decision 4). Shared private-file read and write helpers.
- `src/core/operator/notify-status.ts`: `NotifyStatusV1` is protocol 2 with `relay: 'live'`. Reasons `hc_unavailable` and `relay_stopped` replace `herdr_unavailable`. Delivery state `unsupported` and the plugin log parser are removed. One decoder for the relay delivery record. `NOTIFY_INSTALL_COMMAND` and `NOTIFY_START_COMMAND` are the one source for the command text in the CLI, the server and the UI.
- `src/effects/operator/notify-status.ts`: reads the record, then `hcListAsync(record.labels)`. No live terminal with the record name is `relay_stopped`; an hc failure or timeout is `hc_unavailable`. A config that `decodeNotifyConfig` refuses is `notify_config_unavailable`.
- Bots page (`BotsPage.tsx`, `i18n.ts`, `bots.ts`, fixtures), per the canvas:
  - A live relay shows one ok line, "relay live".
  - `relay_stopped` shows a warn line and the start command.
  - A missing or invalid record shows the install command, which has no `--session`.
  - The Herdr section uses the same install command.
  - The canvas placeholder for the restart command is `repo-harness herdr notify start`.
- Type-only operator changes (decision Q1): `bot-access.ts` herdr section returns `notify_session_missing`; `execution-collector.ts` passes no Herdr session. The classic `herdr --session status` read and its snapshot code in `bot-access.ts` are removed with it. #1478 replaces the section with hc reads.
- `src/core/operator/bot-access.ts` decoder, `server.ts` reason table (`relay_stopped` → start command), `NotifyStatus.tsx` (three classic rows removed).
- `bot-event.mjs` moves to `assets/herdr/github-events/` beside the Worker, with a `.d.mts`. `assertBotEvent` is unchanged. The Worker stage no longer builds a `webhook-notify` directory.
- Deleted: `assets/herdr/webhook-notify/` (plugin, `pane-status.mjs` and `worktree-location.mjs` projections), `src/effects/terminal/herdr-decision.ts`, `src/core/decision/pane-status.{mjs,d.mts}`, `tests/unit/pane-status.test.ts`, and the projection loop in `scripts/sync-helper-sources.ts`.
- Docs: `herdr-notify.md` notify sections and the start command; ADR-0002 path; CHANGELOG Breaking entry (decision 7).

### Deviation from the canvas

In the stopped state the page does not show the channel rows or the relay terminal name. The status contract (decision Q2) carries channel results and the name only with `relay: 'live'`. A stopped relay is an `unavailable` status with the reason `relay_stopped` and no other data. To show them, the contract must change. I did not change it in this PR.

### Shadow decision deletion (decision Q3)

The Clef shadow decision read the pane tail through `herdr pane read`, which has no herdr-core plugin host. Its seven-day record count was unavailable (`docs/researches/clef-shadow-phase0.notes.md:57`), and no other code read its records. It is deleted, not moved.

### hc methods and exit codes

All calls go through `src/effects/terminal/herdr-core.ts` (#1475). No `herdr`, `herdr plugin` or `herdr-app` call remains in the notify path.

| Call | hc command | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `hcEvents` | `hc events --json --label repo-harness.notify=on` | relay stream: snapshot, `missed` snapshot, then `event` notifications (`created`, `labels`, `status`, `turn`, `removed`); heartbeats stay in the transport |
| `hcListAsync` | `hc ls --json --label repo-harness.role=notify-relay` | notify status, async in the operator server |
| `hcList` | same | install, start and doctor; uninstall adds `--all` |
| `hcRun` | `hc run --json --bg --label repo-harness.role=notify-relay --name rh-notify-relay --no-parent -- <bun> <cli> herdr notify relay --home <abs>` | install and start |
| `hcKill`, `hcRm` | `hc get --json -- <t>` (owner label check), then `hc kill --json -- <t>`, `hc rm --json -- <t>` | uninstall |

Exit codes: any non-zero hc exit or timeout is a `HerdrCoreError`. Install, start, uninstall and doctor map it to a fixed message without hc's text (it can hold private paths). The status maps it to `hc_unavailable`. hc documents 3 `not_found`, 7 `needs_target`, 9 `blocked`, 10 `status_mismatch`, 11 `finished`; the notify path does not branch on them.

Each hc CLI call starts a stopped hc core, and no `hc ls` flag prevents it (coordinator decision: accepted). The console status read and doctor therefore show `relay_stopped` after a core stop, and `herdr-notify.md` says so.

Finding from the real run: an hc terminal starts with the core's environment, not the caller's. The relay first read the default home. Install and start pass the home as `--home` (commit 9962ae678).

## Architecture

- `capability.runtime-harness.task-agent-host`: removes `herdr-decision.ts`.
- `component.task-agent-host.core-layer`: removes the `pane-status.{mjs,d.mts}` excludes.

pr1499.body:
## Goal

Task sessions run in herdr-core (`hc`) terminals. hc starts, messages, reads, observes and ends them. The classic Herdr pane, agent and workspace calls are deleted from the task-session path.

Refs #1474
Closes #1476
Depends on #1491 (#1475 transport) and #1492 (#1490 hc install in CI)

## Scope

- In: `src/effects/terminal/task-session*.ts`, `task-worktree-runtime.ts`, the runtime name in the binding projections, `contract-worktree start --herdr-endpoint`. By the scope change in https://github.com/Ancienttwo/repo-harness/issues/1476#issuecomment-6585359634, also the review endpoint: its type and validator, the CLI JSON, and the endpoint construction in the review tests.
- Out: the `--launch` rename and OSC 7501 in the OAR host (#1477), the operator's hc location (#1478), notify (#1479), the classic pin and CI (#1480, #1481), guidance (#1482), and architecture summaries (#1483).
- The board decisions that apply: https://github.com/Ancienttwo/repo-harness/issues/1474#issuecomment-6585114904 (decisions 1, 2 and 4), placement and role https://github.com/Ancienttwo/repo-harness/issues/1476#issuecomment-6585315909, and CI https://github.com/Ancienttwo/repo-harness/issues/1476#issuecomment-6585255700.

## Changes

- **Start.** `startTaskAgent` runs `hc run --bg --no-parent --name task-<20 hex> --cwd <checkout>` with the labels `repo-harness.role=task-session`, `repo-harness.task=<session key>`, `repo-harness.request=<intent id>`, `repo-harness.harness=<kind>` and `repo-harness.notify=on`. `--no-parent` keeps the session alive after its owner ends, and hc types no notes into the caller. No Herdr.app tab or pane is created. To show a session, the operator runs `herdr-app do terminal.keep`. This replaces the issue line "启动：`herdr-app do tab.new` / `pane.split --argv`" (placement decision).
- **Phases.** `intent.json` → `launch-intent.json` → `hc run` → `terminal-created.json` → ready → `provider-created.json` → `binding.json`. A failed or lost `hc run` or ready writes `launch-unknown.json` and is never replayed. An unbound start is cleaned up by its labels with `hc ls --all --label`, so a finished terminal whose run receipt was lost is found too. Before it ends or removes that terminal, cleanup reads it with `hc get`. The name, the full set of intent labels and the recorded provider pid must match; otherwise cleanup fails with `task_agent_terminal_identity_lost` and removes nothing. Only `not_found` counts as an absent terminal.
- **Binding.** `runtime: 'herdr-core'`, `endpoint`, `terminal_id` (hc address), `terminal_name`, `provider` (the terminal's program pid plus `ps` birth identity). The fields `pane_id`, `workspace_id`, `shell` and `agent_name` are removed. `assertTaskBinding` compares hc's address, name, the `repo-harness.*` labels and the program pid, so `process-info` and `agent get` have no counterpart. A label that another tool adds, such as `herdr.space`, does not break the binding.
- **Removed classic steps.** `pane report-agent` is removed: the OAR host writes OSC 7501 itself (decision 3, #1477). `agent rename` is removed: hc names the terminal at `run`.
- **Messages.** `notifyTaskWorktreeMerged` sends with `hcSend`. The owner must be an hc `t<n>` address (a classic `w1:p2` pane id is invalid), and a live repo-harness terminal with `foreground.cwd` in the worktree. An owner without a repo-harness label gives `retained` with reason `owner_unowned`, and nothing is sent. The coordinator then sends the notice by hand, until the seat launch (#1473) labels worker terminals (decision https://github.com/Ancienttwo/repo-harness/issues/1476#issuecomment-6586892733).
- **Close and cancel.** `hc kill` (hangup, then escalation by hc), a wait for the provider's exit, `hc rm`, then `closed.json`. The PID-signal path (`stopCreatedProcess`, `createdProcessGroupAlive`) and the unbound PID receipt are deleted, because hc ends only the terminal it owns.
- **Endpoint.** `HerdrCoreEndpoint {socket, home?}`. `socket` selects the core (`HC_SOCKET`). `home` is the review credential source: review reads its credentials from that directory. hc and task sessions do not get it as HOME. When the caller's `HC_TERMINAL_SOCKET` names another core, `HC_TERMINAL_ID`, `HC_TERMINAL_SOCKET` and `HC_SCOPE` are removed from the hc environment. The classic `HerdrEndpoint` moves to `herdr.ts` for its remaining classic consumers.
- **Spec.** `TaskAgentSpec.parent_pane` is deleted, and the parent terminal check with it. With no window placement the check has no job (same decision). Review keeps its own `parentPane`/`parent_pane` for owner inference, which #1477 migrates. A start request or a start intent whose spec carries `parent_terminal` fails with the retired-record error. A request fails before any session directory exists.
- **Worktree registration.** `task-workspaces/<key>/binding.json` is `{protocol: 2, repository, endpoint}`. hc has no workspace, so registration and `cleanupTaskWorktree` create or close nothing in the core. Cleanup closes the checkout's open roles, then records `closed.json`. `contract-worktree start --herdr-endpoint` takes exactly `{"endpoint":{"socket":...}}`. Any other key, such as a classic `parent_pane` or a `parent_terminal`, fails with the retired-record error.
- **Retired records (decision 4).** A classic binding (`runtime: 'herdr'`), a start intent without `runtime`, a workspace binding with protocol 1, or `open-intent.json` fails with `task_agent_classic_herdr_record_retired: <path>. Classic Herdr sessions are not migrated; archive this record and start the session again.` No migration command and no translator exist. Worktree cleanup validates only the cleaned checkout's intents, so a retired record elsewhere does not block it.
- **Runtime name.** `'herdr'` → `'herdr-core'` in `runner-port.ts`, the sessions and operator decoders, and the admitted task context. TypeScript required the `runner-port.ts` union rename, which the #1477 body lists. #1477 keeps the review `--launch` value.
- **Operator.** `herdr_pane` in the execution state is now `null` for every session, because no classic pane exists. #1478 projects the hc location. The board fixture `src/operator-web/fixtures/dev-activity.ts` names the runtime `herdr-core`. Its sample pane stays, because the page and its decoder still accept one until #1478.
- **Docs.** `docs/CHANGELOG.md` has a Breaking entry. The endpoint file shape is updated in `docs/spec.md` and in the cross-review skill reference.

### hc and herdr-app surface used

Through the typed helpers of `src/effects/terminal/herdr-core.ts` (#1475), all with `--json`, hc 0.1.17. Each single-terminal helper takes only a `t<n>` address, and refuses a terminal without a repo-harness label (`unowned`):

| Call | Use | Error kinds and exit codes relied on |
|---|---|---|
| `hc run --bg --no-parent --name --cwd --label … -- argv` | start | `name_taken`; any failure → ambiguous launch |
| `hc get -- <t>` | identity: address, name, labels, `pid`, `foreground.cwd`, `state` | `not_found` (exit 3) → terminal removed / owner gone |
| `hc ls --all --label …` | find an unbound start's terminal, live or finished | — |
| `hcSend` (`hc get`, then `hc send -- <t> <text>`) | merge notice delivery | `unowned` → `retained` `owner_unowned`; any other failure, including `blocked` (exit 9) and `finished` (exit 11) → `retained`, never replayed |
| `hc kill -- <t>` | end the session | a finished terminal returns success |
| `hc rm -- <t>` | remove the finished terminal | — (an unbound start reads the terminal with `hc get` first, and only `not_found` counts as absent) |

`herdr-app do`: not used (placement decision). `hc read` and `hc wait` are used only by the tests.

## Verification

At 23627c4f5 (this PR's commits, with #1475 at 20e2cbd21 and #1490 at a331018da merged), macOS 26 arm64, hc 0.1.17, bun 1.4.3:

- `bun run check:type`: exit 0.
- `bun run test:files tests/herdr-task-lifecycle.test.ts --timeout 60000 --max-concurrency 1`: 8 pass, 0 fail. With `all: false` in the unbound cleanup, the lost-receipt case fails and lists the finished terminal.
- `bun run test:files tests/effects/task-worktree-closeout-notify.test.ts tests/effects/task-session-admission.test.ts tests/cli/external-source-binding.test.ts tests/effects/external-source-binding.test.ts tests/effects/operator-task-diff.test.ts tests/effects/operator-execution-state.test.ts tests/effects/native-task-session.test.ts tests/effects/herdr-core-transport.test.ts tests/acceptance-receipt.test.ts tests/operator-web/operator-board.test.tsx tests/operator-web/operator-task-diff.test.tsx --timeout 60000 --max-concurrency 1`: 184 pass, 0 fail (7, 4, 2, 9, 25, 20, 13, 9, 39, 50, 6).
- `bun run test:files tests/generic-review.test.ts --timeout 60000 --max-concurrency 1`, run alone: 50 pass, 0 fail.
- `tests/herdr-task-lifecycle.test.ts` starts its own hc core per test: a private HOME, XDG and TMPDIR, `HC_SESSION=task-proof-<hex>`, and the caller's `HC_*` removed. It stops that core in teardown, and it never contacts the default core. CI gets `hc` 0.1.17 from #1490's action, which is merged into this branch.

### Test budget

`git diff --numstat origin/feat/1475-hc-transport...HEAD`: product (src, scripts) +283 / −441; tests +415 / −699, ratio 1.47:1; no new test file. These counts include the merge of #1490's branch, which belongs to #1492.

### Test changes, item by item

`tests/herdr-task-lifecycle.test.ts` moved from `herdr --session` to an isolated hc core. Each dropped case:

- **"Linked task peers survive owner exit… sentinel".** It exercised classic Herdr itself (workspace create, worktree open, split, report-agent, rename, agent prompt/read). The main test now covers the same ground on hc: separate owner processes, hc send delivery, `hc read` output, and a parent terminal that is still live after close.
- **Agent rename blocks close.** hc has no agent names. The name and label tamper cases cover it (`terminal_identity_lost`, nothing killed).
- **PATH-shim `worktree open` failure, linked/primary workspace ids, `workspace_attached`, the vanished/failed-open/ambiguous-open incarnations.** hc has no workspace. The endpoint-changed case and the closed incarnation that moves to history are kept.
- **`stubborn` (TERM ignored, PID KILL).** No PID signals remain. hc escalates, and the `grouped` case covers it.
- **`bind-group-child` (#754).** It is merged into `grouped`: the child starts before ready, the provider is the leader, and both end.
- **`shell-leader`.** No shell exists: the program is the terminal's program.
- **`exitAt` shims on `herdr pane get`, `agent get` and `ps`.** They targeted classic call windows that no longer exist.
- **`split-gap`, `pane-gone`, `cleanup-pending` with `unbound-cleanup.json`.** These reasons and the receipt are deleted. The ready-crash case covers the cleanup of an unbound start by labels.

Cases that the review round added to the same file:

- A foreign `herdr.space` label on the bound terminal does not block the later close.
- A fresh start request with `parent_terminal` is refused, and no session directory is created.
- An unbound recorded terminal that was relabeled with another request id gives `terminal_identity_lost`. The terminal and its program stay. After the label is restored, close succeeds.
- A run whose receipt was lost and whose program then exited: cancel returns `closed`, and `hc ls --all` with the intent label is empty. Without `all`, this case fails with the finished terminal still listed.

The other test files:

- **`tests/helpers/engineer-runtime-fixture.ts`.** The offline double spies the herdr-core functions instead of `herdrCommand`. Its labels come from the same keys and session key as the product.
- **`tests/effects/task-worktree-closeout-notify.test.ts`.**
  - `extra_panes` and the owner pane close are dropped. Cleanup now ends the live owner role itself (`hcKill` and `hcRm` once each).
  - The first notify after a removed owner expects `owner_gone/agent_exited`. `workspace_closed` is now asserted after cleanup.
  - The `'replaced'` agent-to-pane mode is dropped, because notify addresses the owner terminal directly. The `unreachable` and `foreign-cwd` modes are kept.
  - Delivery is asserted as `['send', '--', <terminal>]` with `HC_SOCKET` equal to the endpoint socket.
  - A classic `w1:p2` owner gives `worktree_merge_notice_invalid`.
- **`tests/effects/operator-execution-state.test.ts`.** `herdr_pane` is now `null` and `runtime` is `'herdr-core'`. The "a Herdr pane location needs the session" decoder test is unchanged, but no collector emits a pane until #1478.
- **`tests/generic-review.test.ts`.** The 103-byte check on classic socket paths is dropped, because the hc validator needs only absolute paths. The long UTF-8 root test still passes. `AUTHOR_PANE` is now a valid hc address from the double (`offlineTerminalAddress`).
- **Mechanical changes in the other files.** `{session}` → `{socket, home?}`, `'herdr'` → `'herdr-core'`, `parent_pane` removed from task specs, and `pane_id` → `terminal_id`.

No assertion was weakened to pass. Each change follows a removed classic behavior.

## Architecture
